STUDYQURAN:39:intro/r11.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:39:intro/r11.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:39:intro/r11.claim: The death passage shows disbelievers’ desperate end; verse 53 then emphasizes that God’s mercy and forgiveness remain available even to those who squandered their souls.
STUDYQURAN:39:intro/r11.anchor: A passage on death emphasizes the desperate circumstances of those who disbelieve when they meet their final end

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p522/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p522/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p522/r2.claim: The arrogant attribute God-given wealth and status to their own planning, though earlier people held the same delusion and were seized without their plans helping them.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p522/r2.anchor: they think that the wealth and status which God has bestowed upon them is the result of their own planning

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p209/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p209/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p209/r7.claim: People turn to God in adversity despite worshipping idols, then abandon idols in hardship and call the Lord of heaven and earth, exposing their contradiction.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p209/r7.anchor: تقدم في غير آية كون الإنسان إذا مسه الضر التجأ إلى الله، مع اعتقادهم الأوثان وعبادتها. فإذا أصابتهم شدة، نبذوها ودعوا رب السموات والأرض

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p209/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p209/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p209/r8.claim: The person and harm are generic and blessing covers every pleasing benefit, including relief from harm; an alternative identifies the person as Hudhayfa ibn al-Mughira.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p209/r8.anchor: والإنسان جنس وضر مطلق، والنعمة عامة في جميع ما يسر، ومن ذلك إزالة الضر. وقيل: الإنسان معين، وهو حذيفة بن المغيرة.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p210/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p210/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p210/r1.claim: The author reads ما in إنما as a particle that blocks إن from its usual effect and permits a verbal clause; an alternative treats it as a relative pronoun.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p210/r1.anchor: كافة مهيئة لدخول إن على الجملة الفعلية، وذكر الضمير في أوتيته

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p210/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p210/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p210/r2.claim: The masculine pronoun in أوتيته is justified because blessing can mean wealth or encompass masculine and feminine things.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p210/r2.anchor: وذكر الضمير في أوتيته، وإن كان عائدا على النعمة، لأن معناها مذكر، وهو الأنعام أو المال

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p210/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p210/r3.speaker: قتادة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p210/r3.claim: If ما is relative, the boast means he received wealth through his own knowledge of earning and trade, showing self-admiration.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p210/r3.anchor: قاله قتادة، وفيه إعجاب بالنفس وتعاظم مفرط.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p210/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p210/r4.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p210/r4.claim: Other readings of the boast attribute the gift to God's knowledge of the recipient's deserving it, or to the recipient's own knowledge that his merit would bring it.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p210/r4.anchor: أو على علم من الله في واستحقاق جزائه عند الله، وفي هذا احتراز الله وعجز ومن على الله. أو على علم مني بأني سأعطاه لما في من فضل واستحقاق

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p210/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p210/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p210/r5.claim: Rather, the blessing is a trial that rebuts the claim it was earned through knowledge; the pronoun can return to the gift or its bestowal.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p210/r5.anchor: بل هي فتنة إضراب عن دعواه أنه إنما أوتي على علم، بل تلك النعمة فتنة وابتلاء.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p210/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p210/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p210/r6.claim: The fa in فإذا marks the cause-and-effect reversal: a person who shunned God invokes Him in distress, an inconsistency the passage exposes.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p210/r6.anchor: وكان العطف هنا بالفاء في فإذا، وبالواو في أول السورة لأنها وقعت مسببة عن قوله: وإذا ذكر الله

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p210/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p210/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p210/r7.claim: The earlier wa clause is coordination rather than causation; if فإذا resumes 39:45, intervening verses are an aside reinforcing their reversal and the Prophet's prayer and warning.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p210/r7.anchor: وأما الآية الأولى فلم تقع مسببة، بل ناسبت ما قبلها، فعطفت عليه بالواو، وإذا كانت فإذا متصلة بقوله: وإذا ذكر الله وحده

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p210#2/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p210#2/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p210#2/r2.claim: The author instead links the severe, unexpected punishment to the following portrait of wrongdoers invoking God in distress but denying His gift, then facing the consequences.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p210#2/r2.anchor: والذي يظهر في الربط أنه لما قال: ولو أن للذين ظلموا الآية، كان ذلك إشعارا بما ينال الظالمين من شدة العذاب

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p210#2/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p210#2/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p210#2/r3.claim: Most people fail to know that prosperity is a gradual enticement and a test.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p210#2/r3.anchor: ولكن أكثرهم لا يعلمون: أي أن ذلك استدراج وامتحان.

RAZI-FULL:v26p250/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p250/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p250/r1.claim: Razi describes people who, in poverty or illness, appeal to God and believe only He can remove their distress.
RAZI-FULL:v26p250/r1.anchor: عند الوقوع في الضر الذي هو الفقر والمرض يفزعون إلى الله تعالى

RAZI-FULL:v26p250/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p250/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p250/r2.claim: When granted wealth or health, they credit their own earnings, effort, or medical treatment, contradicting their earlier appeal to God.
RAZI-FULL:v26p250/r2.anchor: زعم أنه إنما حصل ذلك بكسبه وبسبب جهده وجده

RAZI-FULL:v26p250/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p250/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p250/r3.claim: The blessing is a test: gratitude is due when it arrives and patience when it departs, like gold tested by fire; most people miss this purpose.
RAZI-FULL:v26p250/r3.anchor: عند حصولها يجب الشكر ، وعند فواتها يجب الصبر

RAZI-FULL:v26p250/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p250/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p250/r4.claim: Razi calls the brief phrase a fluent, concise exposure of their disgraceful inconsistency in hardship and ease.
RAZI-FULL:v26p250/r4.anchor: قبح طريقتهم فيما هم عليه عند الشدة والرخاء بلفظة وجيزة فصيحة

RAZI-FULL:v26p250/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p250/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p250/r5.claim: The fāʾ here follows the earlier account that they recoil from hearing about God alone but rejoice at mention of partners; it marks their immediate contradiction. The opening-sūra parallel uses wāw because it does not stress immediacy.
RAZI-FULL:v26p250/r5.anchor: ثم ذكر بفاء التعقيب أنهم إذا وقعوا في الضر والبلاء

RAZI-FULL:v26p251/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p251/r1.speaker: الشاعر
RAZI-FULL:v26p251/r1.claim: The unnamed couplet denies that auspicious Jupiter or ill-omened Saturn determines outcomes, attributing decree to the Lord of heaven.
RAZI-FULL:v26p251/r1.anchor: فلا السعد يقضي به المشترى … ولا النحس يقضي علينا زحل

STUDYQURAN:39:49/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:39:49/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:39:49/r1.claim: The pattern of calling on God in hardship and turning away when relieved is repeated elsewhere in the Quran.

STUDYQURAN:39:49/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:39:49/r2.speaker: R
STUDYQURAN:39:49/r2.claim: Turning to God in need, then growing arrogant with blessing, exposes corruption: people acknowledge God alone protects them, then credit their gains to their own striving.
STUDYQURAN:39:49/r2.anchor: they have in effect acknowledged that none but God can protect them from what afflicts them

STUDYQURAN:39:49/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:39:49/r3.speaker: IK, R
STUDYQURAN:39:49/r3.claim: One interpretation is that God gave the blessings because He knew the recipient deserved them.
STUDYQURAN:39:49/r3.anchor: “I was given these blessings because God knew that I deserved them” (IK, R)

STUDYQURAN:39:49/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:39:49/r4.speaker: IK, Q
STUDYQURAN:39:49/r4.claim: Another interpretation is that the recipient claims to have received blessings because of a special position.
STUDYQURAN:39:49/r4.anchor: “because I have a special position” (IK, Q)

STUDYQURAN:39:49/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:39:49/r5.speaker: IK, R
STUDYQURAN:39:49/r5.claim: The claim may mean that the recipient himself knew that he deserved the blessings.
STUDYQURAN:39:49/r5.anchor: “because I myself knew that I deserved them”(IK, R)

STUDYQURAN:39:49/r6.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:39:49/r6.speaker: Q, R
STUDYQURAN:39:49/r6.claim: Alternatively, the speaker says his own knowledge earned him the benefit.
STUDYQURAN:39:49/r6.anchor: “because my own knowledge earned this benefit for me” (Q, R)

STUDYQURAN:39:49/r7.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:39:49/r7.speaker: Q
STUDYQURAN:39:49/r7.claim: A further interpretation is that the blessing came because of knowledge God had taught the recipient.
STUDYQURAN:39:49/r7.anchor: “because of some knowledge that God has taught me” (Q)

STUDYQURAN:39:49/r8.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:39:49/r8.speaker: R
STUDYQURAN:39:49/r8.claim: Blessings are a trial requiring gratitude while they last and patience when they disappear.
STUDYQURAN:39:49/r8.anchor: Such blessings are a trial from God because one must manifest gratitude upon receiving them and patience upon their disappearance (R)

BURSEVI:v8p91#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p91#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p91#2/r1.claim: The verse describes what most people do rather than every human being without exception.
BURSEVI:v8p91#2/r1.anchor: إخبار عن الجنس بما يفعله غالب أفراده

BURSEVI:v8p91#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p91#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p91#2/r2.claim: The fa orders this response after the preceding description: polytheists recoil from God's mention alone but rejoice at idols, yet appeal to God when hardship strikes.
BURSEVI:v8p91#2/r2.anchor: والفاء : لترتيب ما بعدها على ما قبلها

BURSEVI:v8p91#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p91#2/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p91#2/r3.claim: This reversal makes disbelief the means of turning to God in place of faith, though faith should be the means of seeking Him.
BURSEVI:v8p91#2/r3.anchor: حيث جعلوا الكفر سببا في الالتجاء إلى الله بأن أقاموه مقام الإيمان

BURSEVI:v8p91#3/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p91#3/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p91#3/r1.claim: Khawwalnah means giving a blessing as a favor; it is not used for a recompense.
BURSEVI:v8p91#3/r1.anchor: أعطيناه إياها تفضلا ، فإن التخويل مختص بما كان بطريق التفضل

BURSEVI:v8p91#3/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p91#3/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p91#3/r2.claim: One reading of “upon knowledge” is that the person knows the means by which the blessing was acquired.

BURSEVI:v8p91#3/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p91#3/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p91#3/r3.claim: A second reading is that the person knew he would receive the blessing because of his merit and deserving.
BURSEVI:v8p91#3/r3.anchor: أو بأني سأعطاه لما لي من الفضل والاستحقاق

BURSEVI:v8p91#3/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p91#3/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p91#3/r4.claim: A third reading is that God knew the person deserved the blessing.
BURSEVI:v8p91#3/r4.anchor: أو على علم من الله باستحقاقي

BURSEVI:v8p91#3/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p91#3/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p91#3/r5.claim: The pronoun may refer to the relative expression أن الذي أوتيته or to the blessing if the particle إن is taken as redundant; masculine form represents a thing or portion of a blessing.

BURSEVI:v8p91#3/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p91#3/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p91#3/r6.claim: God rejects the claim: the blessing is instead a trial testing whether the person gives thanks or disbelieves, like gold tested in fire for its quality.
BURSEVI:v8p91#3/r6.anchor: أي : محنة وابتلاء له أيشكر أم يكفر

BURSEVI:v8p91#4/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p91#4/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p91#4/r1.claim: Most people do not know that a bestowed blessing is a test and a gradual enticement.

TAB-FULL:v20p221/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p221/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v20p221/r1.claim: When distress strikes, a person calls on God for help; after God relieves it with ease, wealth, health, and well-being, the person claims the favor came through his own knowledge and merit.
TAB-FULL:v20p221/r1.anchor: فإذا أصاب الإنسان بؤس وشدة دعانا مستغيثا بنا من جهة ما أصابه من الضر

TAB-FULL:v20p221/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p221/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v20p221/r2.claim: The person claims he received prosperity because God knew he deserved it through his distinction and approved deeds; عندي means in my own estimation.
TAB-FULL:v20p221/r2.anchor: يعني على علم من الله بأني له أهل لشرفي

TAB-FULL:v20p221/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p221/r3.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v20p221/r3.claim: Mujahid glosses خولناه as “We gave him.”
TAB-FULL:v20p221/r3.anchor: عن ابن أبي نجيح، عن مجاهد، قوله: {إذا خولناه نعمة منا}

TAB-FULL:v20p221/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p221/r4.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v20p221/r4.claim: Qatada understands the claim as meaning that the favor came because of good standing in the recipient's own estimation.
TAB-FULL:v20p221/r4.anchor: عن قتادة، قوله: {ثم إذا خولناه نعمة منا}

TAB-FULL:v20p222/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p222/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v20p222/r1.claim: The favor given after distress is a trial and test for the people who receive it.
TAB-FULL:v20p222/r1.anchor: بل عطيتنا إياهم تلك النعمة من بعد الضر الذي كانوا فيه فتنة لهم

TAB-FULL:v20p222/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p222/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v20p222/r2.claim: Most people fail to understand why they received the favor because of ignorance and poor judgment.

TAB-FULL:v20p222/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p222/r3.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v20p222/r3.claim: Qatada glosses فتنة here as a trial or affliction.

TABATABAI:39:49/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:39:49/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:39:49/r5.claim: The verse explains the preceding description of wrongdoers; its opening faʾ links the explanation to what came before.
TABATABAI:39:49/r5.anchor: الآية في مقام التعليل البياني لما تقدم من وصف الظالمين

TABATABAI:39:49/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:39:49/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:39:49/r6.claim: Human nature follows desire and is deluded by worldly blessings and visible means: in hardship people turn sincerely to God, but after relief they credit their own skill and forget that bounty is a test.
TABATABAI:39:49/r6.anchor: فالإنسان حليف النسيان إذا مسه الضر أقبل إلى ربه وأخلص له

TABATABAI:39:49/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:39:49/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:39:49/r7.claim: Ḍurr here means illness or hardship.

TABATABAI:39:49/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:39:49/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:39:49/r8.claim: He calls upon God alone in supplication and cuts himself off from others.
TABATABAI:39:49/r8.anchor: أي خصنا بالدعاء وانقطع عن غيرنا

TABATABAI:39:49/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:39:49/r9.speaker: author
TABATABAI:39:49/r9.claim: Khawwalah means to give as a gift; “a bounty from Us” marks it as an actual bounty.
TABATABAI:39:49/r9.anchor: التخويل الإعطاء على نحو الهبة، وتقييد النعمة

TABATABAI:39:49/r10.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:39:49/r10.speaker: author
TABATABAI:39:49/r10.claim: The pronoun in “I was given it” refers to the bounty as a thing or property, reflecting the speaker’s refusal to acknowledge it as a gift from God.
TABATABAI:39:49/r10.anchor: للنعمة بما أنه شيء أو مال والعناية في ذلك

TABATABAI:39:49/r11.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:39:49/r11.speaker: author
TABATABAI:39:49/r11.claim: By calling it a bounty “from Us” and then saying merely “I was given it,” the Qur’an captures the speaker’s detachment of the benefit from its giver.
TABATABAI:39:49/r11.anchor: فيسميها شيئا أو مالا ونحوه ولا يسميها نعمة

TABATABAI:39:49/r12.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:39:49/r12.speaker: author
TABATABAI:39:49/r12.claim: In context, the speaker means “through my own knowledge”: his expertise in earning a living, acquiring wealth, and accumulating money.
TABATABAI:39:49/r12.anchor: والملائم لسياق الآية أن يكون معنى

TABATABAI:39:49-52/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:39:49-52/r1.speaker: قيل
TABATABAI:39:49-52/r1.claim: One view says the speaker received the bounty because God knew he was good and deserved it; another says he knew God was pleased with him.
TABATABAI:39:49-52/r1.anchor: وقيل المراد إنما أوتيته على علم من الله بخير عندي

TABATABAI:39:49-52/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:39:49-52/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:39:49-52/r2.claim: Al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī rejects both alternatives because they do not fit the preceding explanation of the statement.

TABATABAI:39:49-52/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:39:49-52/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:39:49-52/r3.claim: The bounty God gives is a trial and examination, though most people do not know this.
TABATABAI:39:49-52/r3.anchor: أي بل النعمة التي خولناه منا فتنة

TABATABAI:39:49-52/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:39:49-52/r4.speaker: قيل
TABATABAI:39:49-52/r4.claim: Alternative readings say the bounty itself is a punishment, or that the boastful statement is a trial for which its speaker is punished; al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī finds both far-fetched, especially the latter.
TABATABAI:39:49-52/r4.anchor: وقيل معناه بل تلك النعمة عذاب لهم، وقيل المعنى

TABRISI:39:46-50/r13.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:39:46-50/r13.speaker: author
TABRISI:39:46-50/r13.claim: When illness or distress touches a person, he calls sincerely as a Muslim, knowing only God can remove it.
TABRISI:39:46-50/r13.anchor: من مرض أو شدة { دعانا } واستغاث بنا مسلما مخلصا

TABRISI:39:46-50/r14.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:39:46-50/r14.speaker: author
TABRISI:39:46-50/r14.claim: God's granting a favor means giving health, bodily well-being, abundant livelihood, or another blessing.
TABRISI:39:46-50/r14.anchor: أي أعطيناه نعمة من الصحة في الجسم والسعة في الرزق

TABRISI:39:46-50/r15.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:39:46-50/r15.speaker: الحسن والجبائي
TABRISI:39:46-50/r15.claim: Al-Ḥasan and al-Jubbāʾī say the speaker claims he obtained the blessing through his own knowledge, effort, and skill, exposing ignorance about the sources of benefit and harm.
TABRISI:39:46-50/r15.anchor: قال إنما أوتيته بعلمي وجلدي وحيلتي عن الحسن والجبائي

TABRISI:39:46-50/r16.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:39:46-50/r16.speaker: قتادة ومقاتل
TABRISI:39:46-50/r16.claim: Qatāda and Muqātil explain the claim as a report of knowledge God knew the person possessed.
TABRISI:39:46-50/r16.anchor: على علم على خبر علمه الله عندي عن قتادة ومقاتل

TABRISI:39:46-50/r17.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:39:46-50/r17.speaker: قيل
TABRISI:39:46-50/r17.claim: Another view says the speaker thinks the blessing came because God approves of him.
TABRISI:39:46-50/r17.anchor: وثالثها: على علم يرضاه عني فلذلك أتاني ما أتاني من النعم

TABRISI:39:46-50/r18.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:39:46-50/r18.speaker: author
TABRISI:39:46-50/r18.claim: The blessing is a trial that reveals whether the recipient is grateful or patient, with recompense according to the response.
TABRISI:39:46-50/r18.anchor: أي بلية واختبار يبتليه الله بها فيظهر كيف شكره أو صبره

TABRISI:39:46-50/r19.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:39:46-50/r19.speaker: قيل
TABRISI:39:46-50/r19.claim: An alternative says the blessing itself becomes punishment when they attribute it to themselves.
TABRISI:39:46-50/r19.anchor: وقيل: معناه هذه النعمة فتنة أي عذاب لهم إذا أضافوها إلى أنفسهم

TABRISI:39:46-50/r20.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:39:46-50/r20.speaker: قيل
TABRISI:39:46-50/r20.claim: Another alternative takes the boastful statement itself as their trial, because they will be punished for saying it.
TABRISI:39:46-50/r20.anchor: وقيل: معناه هذه المقالة التي قالوها فتنة لهم لأنهم يعاقبون عليها

TABRISI:39:46-50/r21.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:39:46-50/r21.speaker: author
TABRISI:39:46-50/r21.claim: Most do not distinguish affliction from blessing.

TABRISI:39:46-50/r22.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:39:46-50/r22.speaker: قيل
TABRISI:39:46-50/r22.claim: Another explanation is that they do not know all blessings come from God, even when acquired through human causes.
TABRISI:39:46-50/r22.anchor: وقيل: لا يعلمون أن النعم كلها من الله وإن حصلت بأسباب

THALABI:v8p240/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p240/r2.speaker: سفيان
THALABI:v8p240/r2.claim: Sufyan reads the warning as applying to people who seek reputation, repeating, Woe to the show-offs.
THALABI:v8p240/r2.anchor: قال سفيان: وقرأ هذه الآية: ويل لأهل الريا ويل لأهل الريا.

THALABI:v8p240/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p240/r4.speaker: author
THALABI:v8p240/r4.claim: The afflicted person receives a blessing from God and boasts that God gave it because He knows he deserves it.
THALABI:v8p240/r4.anchor: قال إنما أوتيته على علم من الله بأني له أهل

THALABI:v8p240/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p240/r5.speaker: قتادة
THALABI:v8p240/r5.claim: Qatada glosses the boast as meaning, on account of the good I have.

THALABI:v8p240/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p240/r6.speaker: author
THALABI:v8p240/r6.claim: The pronoun refers to the blessing: the blessing is a trial.

THALABI:v8p240/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p240/r7.speaker: الحسين بن الفضل
THALABI:v8p240/r7.claim: Al-Husayn ibn al-Fadl instead takes the pronoun to refer to the person's boastful utterance, which is a trial.
THALABI:v8p240/r7.anchor: وقال الحسين بن الفضل: بل كلمته التي قالها فتنة.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:39:49-50/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:39:49-50/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:39:49-50/r1.claim: The boastful recipient says he was given wealth because of his own distinction and merit, believing he knew he would receive it through deserving it.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:39:49-50/r1.anchor: أعطيته على شرف وفضل، وكنت علمت أني سأعطى هذا باستحقاقي

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:39:49-50/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:39:49-50/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:39:49-50/r2.claim: The gift is a test from God to see whether the servant gives thanks or disbelieves.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:39:49-50/r2.anchor: أي: تلك العطية فتنة من الله تعالى يبتلي به العبد ليشكر أو يكفر

ELMALILI:39:42-52/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:39:42-52/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:39:42-52/r1.claim: He renders the pattern as a person praying to God in distress, then claiming a blessing was given because of his knowledge; the blessing is a test.
ELMALILI:39:42-52/r1.anchor: Fakat insana bir sıkıntı dokunuverince Bize yalvarır, sonra kendisine tarafımızdan bir nimet bahşediverdiğimiz zaman da “o bana bir bilgi üzerine verildi” der.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:49/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:49/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:49/r1.claim: The passage criticizes blaming God for adversity while claiming blessings for oneself; earlier deniers and the pagan Arabs addressed as “these” in verse 51 acted this way and will suffer for their own evil acquisitions.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:49/r1.anchor: Kötülüğü Allah’a nisbet ederken nimeti, iyiliği kendinden bilme tarzındaki yanlış telakki eleştirilmekte; gerek eski inkârcı toplulukların gerekse 51. âyette “bunlar” şeklinde kendilerine işaret edilen putperest Araplar’ın bu telakkiye göre davrandıkları

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:49/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:49/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:49/r2.claim: Good and bad events occur only by God’s permission and will, so both good and evil ultimately come from God; human acts shaped by intention and choice are a person’s own acquisition, with consequences proportionate to responsibility.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:49/r2.anchor: Aslında Allah’ın izni ve iradesi olmadan evrende hiçbir olay gerçekleşmediği gibi insanlar da herhangi bir iyi veya kötü durumla karşılaşmazlar. Bu açıdan iyilik de kötülük de Allah’tandır (bk. en-Nisâ 4/78).

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:49/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:49/r3.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:49/r3.claim: The Qur’an attributes human acts and conditions such as good, evil, blessing, and hardship to God or to people according to context; the blessing granted here is a test, passed when used in accordance with God’s pleasure and commands.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:49/r3.anchor: 49. âyete göre nimetin verilmesi bir imtihandır; onu Allah’ın rızasına ve hükümlerine uygun olarak değerlendirenler imtihanı kazanmış, aksine hareket edenler de kaybetmiştir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:49/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:49/r4.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:49/r4.claim: Verse 52’s example of provision shows that both abundance and hardship depend on God’s will and decree.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:49/r4.anchor: 52. âyette rızık örneğinden hareketle bolluğun da sıkıntının da Allah’ın irade ve takdirine bağlı olduğu ortaya konmuştur.

BURHAN:v3p59/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p59/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p59/r1.claim: The prayer “Say: O God, Creator of the heavens and earth” is a parenthesis interrupting the passage from people recoiling at mention of God to their claim when relief comes.
BURHAN:v3p59/r1.anchor: وقوله ﴿ قل اللهم فاطر السماوات والأرض ﴾ 3 إلى قوله ﴿ وحاق بهم ما كانوا به يستهزؤون ﴾ اعتراض في أثناء الكلام

BURHAN:v3p59/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p59/r2.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p59/r2.claim: The harmed polytheist’s turning to God contradicts his recoil from divine unity, so the fa-linked clause exposes his inconsistency; the intervening material is separated from the causal connection and joined by wāw for general coordination.
BURHAN:v3p59/r2.anchor: وذلك لأن قوله ﴿ فإذا مس الإنسان ضر ﴾ سبب عن قوله ﴿ وإذا ذكر الله وحده اشمأزت ﴾

SULAMI:v2p201/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p201/r1.speaker: الجنيد
SULAMI:v2p201/r1.claim: Al-Junayd says a knower sees personal affliction as mercy; true harm is hardness and tarnish in the heart, while blessing is the heart’s turning to God, and claiming to deserve a blessing denies it.
SULAMI:v2p201/r1.anchor: قال الجنيد - رحمة الله عليه - : من ير البلاء ضرا فليس بعارف فإن العارف من يرى الضر على نفسه رحمة

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p403/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p403/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p403/r1.claim: With ḍamma, ḍurr means hardship and affliction; with fatḥa, ḍarr is the opposite of benefit.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p403/r1.anchor: الضر : بضم الضاد [ هو ] الشدة والبلاء . وبفتحها : ضد النفع .

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p403/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p403/r2.speaker: ابن فارس
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p403/r2.claim: Ibn Fāris gives ḍurr the sense of emaciation.

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p403/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p403/r3.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p403/r3.claim: The source notes a form for marrying a woman while another is her co-wife; muḍirr is a woman with co-wives and ḍarīr is someone impaired in sight or body.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p403/r3.anchor: والضر : بكسر الضاد ، تزوج المرأة على ضرة . يقال : نكحت فلانة على ضر ، أي : على امرأة قبلها .

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p403/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p403/r4.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p403/r4.claim: One Qurʾanic sense of ḍurr is scant rainfall, as when people call on God after hardship.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p403/r4.anchor: أحدها : قلة المطر . ومنه قوله تعالى في يونس : ﴿ وإذا أذقنا الناس رحمة من بعد ضراء مستهم ﴾

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p403/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p403/r5.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p403/r5.claim: A second sense is illness, as in Job’s affliction and a person calling on God when harmed.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p403/r5.anchor: والثاني : المرض . ومنه قوله تعالى في الأنبياء

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p403/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p403/r6.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p403/r6.claim: A third sense is terrors of the sea, where those called besides God are lost from view.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p403/r6.anchor: والثالث : أهوال البحر . ومنه قوله تعالى في بني إسرائيل : ﴿ وإذا مسكم الضر في البحر ضل من تدعون إلا إياه ﴾

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p403/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p403/r7.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p403/r7.claim: A fourth sense is need, prompting people to cry out to God.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p403/r7.anchor: والرابع : الحاجة . ومنه قوله تعالى في النحل : ﴿ ثم إذا مسكم الضر فإليه تجأرون ﴾

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p403/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p403/r8.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p403/r8.claim: A fifth sense is hunger, as in Joseph’s brothers describing family hardship.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p403/r8.anchor: والخامس : الجوع . ومنه قوله تعالى في سورة يوسف : ^ ( مسنا وأهلنا الضر ) ^

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p403/r9.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p403/r9.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p403/r9.claim: The final sense is loss or harm, specifically the form with fatḥa on ḍād; these verses say people cannot harm God.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p403/r9.anchor: والسادس : النقصان . ومنه قوله تعالى في آل عمران : ^ ( فلن يضر الله شيئا ) ^

FARRA:v2p419/r6.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p419/r6.speaker: author
FARRA:v2p419/r6.claim: The feminine pronoun agrees with fitna; masculine huwa fitna is also valid, as the Qur'an elsewhere uses masculine hādhā with feminine raḥma.
FARRA:v2p419/r6.anchor: خرجت (هي) بالتأنيث لتأنيث الفتنة. ولو قيل: بل هو فتنة لكان صوابا

FARRA:v2p419/r7.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p419/r7.speaker: author
FARRA:v2p419/r7.claim: The feminine pronoun in qālahā refers to an implied feminine word, such as kalima; masculine qālahu would also be correct.
FARRA:v2p419/r7.anchor: وكذلك قوله: (قد قالها الذين من قبلهم) أنثت إرادة الكلمة

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p264/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p264/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p264/r1.claim: With fatḥa on ḍād, الضر is the opposite of benefit; it can mean inability to bring gain or avert harm.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p264/r1.anchor: الضر: بفتح الضاد- ضد النفع، قال الله عز وجل: هل يسمعونكم إذ تدعون أو ينفعونكم أو يضرون

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p264/r2.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p264/r2.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p264/r2.claim: الضر can also mean hardship or affliction.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p264/r2.anchor: والضر: الشدة والبلاء، كقوله: وإن يمسسك الله بضر

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p264/r3.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p264/r3.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p264/r3.claim: One form of hardship is drought: the mercy after hardship in the cited verse means rain after drought and barrenness.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p264/r3.anchor: فمن الشدة: قحط المطر، قال الله تعالى: وإذا أذقنا الناس رحمة من بعد ضراء

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p264/r4.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p264/r4.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p264/r4.claim: الضر can denote the terror of danger at sea.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p264/r4.anchor: ومنه: الهول، كقوله: وإذا مسكم الضر في البحر

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p264/r5.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p264/r5.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p264/r5.claim: The word can mean illness, as in Job's complaint and the verse about a person in distress calling on God.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p264/r5.anchor: ومنه المرض، كقول أيوب عليه السلام: أني مسني الضر

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p264/r6.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p264/r6.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p264/r6.claim: الضر can also mean loss or diminution, as in the statement that disbelievers will not harm God at all.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p264/r6.anchor: ومنه النقص، كقوله تعالى: لن يضروا الله شيئا وسيحبط أعمالهم

NAHHAS:v4p15/r2.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p15/r2.speaker: أبو إسحاق
NAHHAS:v4p15/r2.claim: Abu Ishaq explains the boast as receiving the gift through merit and foreknowledge that it would be granted.
NAHHAS:v4p15/r2.anchor: قال أبو إسحاق أي على شرف وفضل يجب لي به هذا الذي أعطيته

NAHHAS:v4p15/r3.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p15/r3.speaker: الفراء
NAHHAS:v4p15/r3.claim: Al-Farra says هي is feminine because فتنة is feminine; masculine هو فتنة is also possible.
NAHHAS:v4p15/r3.anchor: قال الفراء أنث لتأنيث الفتنة ولو كان بل هو فتنة لجاز

NAHHAS:v4p15/r4.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p15/r4.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v4p15/r4.claim: The implied sense is rather, I gave it as a trial.
NAHHAS:v4p15/r4.anchor: قال أبو جعفر التقدير بل أعطيته فتنة

NAHHAS:v4p15/r5.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p15/r5.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v4p15/r5.claim: Most do not know that wealth is a test; alternatively their conduct is that of the ignorant.
NAHHAS:v4p15/r5.anchor: أي لا يعلمون أن إعطاءهم المال اختبار وقيل عملهم عمل من لا يعلم

SAMIN-DURR:39:49/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:39:49/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:39:49/r1.claim: In إنما, ما may be an extra particle that makes إن restrictive, or a relative pronoun; the construction admits both parses.
SAMIN-DURR:39:49/r1.anchor: يجوز أن تكون " ما " مهيئة زائدة على " إن " نحو: إنما قام زيد، وأن تكون موصولة

SAMIN-DURR:39:49/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:39:49/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:39:49/r2.claim: If ما is relative, its pronoun resumes it: he says what he received was based on his own knowledge or God's knowledge that he deserved it.
SAMIN-DURR:39:49/r2.anchor: أي: إن الذي أوتيته على علم مني أو على علم من الله في، أي: أستحق/ ذلك.

SAMIN-DURR:39:49/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:39:49/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:39:49/r3.claim: The pronoun in بل هي refers to the blessing; it is first mentioned by meaning as الإنعام, then treated as feminine according to its form. Others take it as the state or bestowal.
SAMIN-DURR:39:49/r3.anchor: الضمير للنعمة. ذكرها أولا في قوله: " إنما أوتيته لأنها بمعنى الإنعام، وأنث هنا اعتبارا بلفظها.

ZAJJAJ:v4p357/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p357/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p357/r1.claim: Khawwalnāhu means that God gave him the blessing as a favor; any gift given without compensation is called a bestowal.
ZAJJAJ:v4p357/r1.anchor: أعطيناه ذلك تفضلا، وكل من أعطى على غير جزاء فقد خول

ZAJJAJ:v4p357/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p357/r2.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p357/r2.claim: The recipient claims that his distinction and merit entitle him to the gift and that he knew he would receive it.
ZAJJAJ:v4p357/r2.anchor: أي أعطيته على شرف وفضل يجب له به هذا الذي أعطيت، فقد علمت أني ساعطى هدى

ZAJJAJ:v4p357/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p357/r3.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p357/r3.claim: God says the gift is a trial and test, by which the servant is tested to see whether he gives thanks or disbelieves.
ZAJJAJ:v4p357/r3.anchor: أي تلك العطية فتنة من الله وبلوى يبتلى بها العبد ليشكر أو يكفر

ASAD-NOTES:39:49#n55/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:39:49#n55/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:39:49#n55/r1.claim: The claim of being given prosperity by one's "knowledge" means attributing it to one's own ability and shrewdness.
ASAD-NOTES:39:49#n55/r1.anchor: Lit., "knowledge" - i.e., "my prosperity is due to my own ability and shrewdness": see the first sentence of 28:78 and the corresponding note.

ASAD-NOTES:39:49#n55/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:39:49#n55/r2.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:39:49#n55/r2.claim: Asad contrasts Qarun's version of this boast in 28:78 with the earlier-revealed present passage, where it characterizes humanity generally; 7:189-190 show the same tendency in connection with parenthood.
ASAD-NOTES:39:49#n55/r2.anchor: in the present instance - which is by far the earlier in the chronology of Qur'anic revelation

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p552/r9.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p552/r9.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p552/r9.claim: He should explain the transient nature of worldly success to those who take pride in it.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p552/r9.anchor: if they show arrogance on their worldly successes, then he should explain their transient nature to them.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p561/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p561/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p561/r1.claim: As already explained in 39:8, a person calls on God in hardship but, after relief, forgets God and the hardship and credits another person or his own planning and science for the blessing.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p561/r1.anchor: once the Almighty relieves him of this hardship and blesses him with His favours, man forgets both God and the hardship

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p561/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p561/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p561/r2.claim: Crediting blessings to another person or oneself is shirk: God alone grants them, while other people are only means and human abilities and science are gifts whose success depends on His permission.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p561/r2.anchor: Both these cases are nothing but polytheism; this is because the favour a person receives is from God alone

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p561/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p561/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p561/r3.claim: Every favor tests whether a person gives thanks or responds with arrogance; most people miss this and fall into shirk and anarchy, as the story of Qarun illustrates.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p561/r3.anchor: through them He actually tries and tests His servants whether they show gratitude to Him or show arrogance and haughtiness.

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p174#3/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p174#3/r1.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p174#3/r1.claim: Qatāda glosses the claim “I was given it through knowledge” as “because of good I have.”
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p174#3/r1.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله ﴿ إنما أوتيته على علم عندي ﴾ قال على خير عندي

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p178#2/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p178#2/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p178#2/r2.claim: خولناه نعمة means He granted him a favor at the outset, without repayment; the verb is not used for a reward.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p178#2/r2.anchor: خوله النعمة: أي أعطاه ابتداء من غير مجازاة، ولا يقال في الجراء خول.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p178#2/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p178#2/r3.speaker: زهير
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p178#2/r3.claim: Zuhayr's line uses استخولوا and يخولوا for giving or receiving wealth.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p178#2/r3.anchor: قال زهير: هنالك إن يستخولوا المال يخولوا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p178#2/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p178#2/r4.speaker: أبو النجم
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p178#2/r4.claim: Abu al-Najm's verse uses خول in a description of someone who gave generously and was not stingy.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p178#2/r4.anchor: وقال أبو النجم: أعطى فلم يبخل ولم يبخل

ALUSI-FULL:v24p12#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v24p12#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v24p12#2/r1.claim: The subject is humankind generally; the following plural most of them supports a generic, rather than individual, reference.
ALUSI-FULL:v24p12#2/r1.anchor: وهذا ظاهر في أن المراد بالإنسان الجنس غذ لو أريد العهد لقيل لكنه لا يعلم

ALUSI-FULL:v24p12#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v24p12#2/r2.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v24p12#2/r2.claim: A reported alternative identifies the person as Hudhayfa ibn al-Mughira.
ALUSI-FULL:v24p12#2/r2.anchor: وقيل : المراد بالإنسان حذيفة بن المغيرة

ALUSI-FULL:v24p12#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v24p12#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v24p12#2/r3.claim: Khawwalnāhu means We bestowed the blessing on him as a favor.

ALUSI-FULL:v24p12#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v24p12#2/r4.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v24p12#2/r4.claim: Some restrict takhwīl to gifts given freely, not recompense.
ALUSI-FULL:v24p12#2/r4.anchor: فإن التخويل على ما قيل مختص به لا يطلق على ما أعطى جزاء

ALUSI-FULL:v24p12#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v24p12#2/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v24p12#2/r5.claim: The boast may mean the recipient knew how to earn the blessing, knew he deserved it, or knew God knew he merited it.
ALUSI-FULL:v24p12#2/r5.anchor: على علم مني بوجوه كسبه أو بأني سأعطاه لمالي من الإستحقاق أو على علم من الله تعالى بي وباستيجابي

ALUSI-FULL:v24p12#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v24p12#2/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v24p12#2/r6.claim: Innamā makes the boast exclusive: he claims he received it only because of knowledge.
ALUSI-FULL:v24p12#2/r6.anchor: وإنما للحصر أي ما أوتيته لشيء من الأشياء إلا لأجل علم

ALUSI-FULL:v24p12#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v24p12#2/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v24p12#2/r7.claim: The pronoun refers to the blessing; its masculine form is explained by construing the feminine blessing as a thing, a verbal noun, wealth, or by masculine predominance.
ALUSI-FULL:v24p12#2/r7.anchor: والهاء للنعمة والتذكير لتأوليها بشيء من النعم

ALUSI-FULL:v24p12#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v24p12#2/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v24p12#2/r8.claim: A possible reading treats innamā as a relative expression, meaning what I received is based on knowledge; al-Ālūsī deems it unlikely because the Qurʾānic spelling joins it.
ALUSI-FULL:v24p12#2/r8.anchor: ويبعد موصوليتها كتابتها متصلة في المصاحف

ALUSI-FULL:v24p12#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v24p12#2/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v24p12#2/r9.claim: The rebuttal says the blessing is a trial testing whether its recipient gives thanks or is ungrateful.
ALUSI-FULL:v24p12#2/r9.anchor: بل ما أوتيه امتحان له أيشكر أم يكفر

ALUSI-FULL:v24p12#2/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v24p12#2/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v24p12#2/r10.claim: The feminine pronoun may follow the word niʿmah after its meaning was considered first; alternatives make it agree with the predicate or refer to the act of granting.
ALUSI-FULL:v24p12#2/r10.anchor: والضمير للنعمة باعتبار لفظها كما أن الأول لها باعتبار معناها

ALUSI-FULL:v24p12#2/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v24p12#2/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v24p12#2/r11.claim: A reading with masculine agreement still refers to the blessing, or alternatively to the act of giving.
ALUSI-FULL:v24p12#2/r11.anchor: وقريء بالتذكير فهو للنعمة أيضا كالذي مر أو للإتيان

ALUSI-FULL:v24p12#2/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v24p12#2/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v24p12#2/r12.claim: Calling the blessing a trial, though it is an instrument of testing, intensifies the expression.
ALUSI-FULL:v24p12#2/r12.anchor: أخبر عنه بالفتنة مع أنه آلهة لها لقصد المبالغة

ALUSI-FULL:v24p12#2/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v24p12#2/r13.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v24p12#2/r13.claim: The shift from the human singular to most of them confirms that al-insān is generic; making it a specific person here would require a strained pronoun shift.
ALUSI-FULL:v24p12#2/r13.anchor: وإرادة العهد هناك وإرجاع الضمير للمطلق هنا على أنه استخدام نظير عندي درهم ونصفه تكلف

ALUSI-FULL:v24p12#2/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v24p12#2/r14.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v24p12#2/r14.claim: The fa links this response to the preceding account of aversion to mentioning God alone: in distress they call the very God whose mention they shunned, rather than the idols they welcomed.
ALUSI-FULL:v24p12#2/r14.anchor: حيث أنهم يشمئزون عن ذكر الله تعالى وحده ويستبشرون بذكر الآلهة فإذا مسهم ضر دعوا من اشمأزوا من ذكره

ALUSI-FULL:v24p12#2/r15.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v24p12#2/r15.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v24p12#2/r15.claim: The fa is a mocking, rebuking connective that exposes their contradiction and reversal; al-Ālūsī compares it to someone who mistreats another but asks that person for help when needy.
ALUSI-FULL:v24p12#2/r15.anchor: والغرض منه التهكم والتحميق وفيه ذمهم بالمناقضة والتعكيس

ALUSI-FULL:v24p12#2/r16.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v24p12#2/r16.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v24p12#2/r16.claim: An alternative takes the fa causally: mentioning the result entails its cause; this may repeat the next verse unless one occurrence is worldly and the other belongs to the afterlife.
ALUSI-FULL:v24p12#2/r16.anchor: وقيل : يجوز أن تكون للسببية داخلة على السبب لأن ذكر المسبب يقتضي ذكر سببه

ALUSI-FULL:v24p12#2/r17.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v24p12#2/r17.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v24p12#2/r17.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī treats the intervening clauses as parenthetical and strengthening the censure; Abū Ḥayyān calls this strained and Abū ʿAlī rejects parentheticals of two clauses, but al-Ālūsī defends the construction with Arabic usage.
ALUSI-FULL:v24p12#2/r17.anchor: وزعم أبو حيان أن في ذلك تكلفا واعتراضا بأكثر من جملتين وأبو علي الفارسي

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p124#2/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p124#2/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p124#2/r2.claim: Here ḍurr means hardship or distress.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p124#2/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p124#2/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p124#2/r3.claim: Khawwalnāhu means that God gave him the blessing.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p124#2/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p124#2/r4.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p124#2/r4.claim: The person claims he received the blessing because God knew he deserved it.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p124#2/r4.anchor: أي: على علم من الله أني له أهل

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p124#2/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p124#2/r5.speaker: مقاتل
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p124#2/r5.claim: Muqātil takes the claim to mean that it came through a good quality God knew the person possessed.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p124#2/r5.anchor: وقال مقاتل: على خير علمه الله عندي

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p124#2/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p124#2/r6.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p124#2/r6.claim: The feminine pronoun is used because the intended noun is al-inʿām, the act of bestowing the blessing.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p124#2/r6.anchor: وذكر الكناية لأن المراد من النعمة الإنعام

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p124#2/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p124#2/r7.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p124#2/r7.claim: The blessing is a divine trial, gradual enticement, and affliction.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p124#2/r7.anchor: استدراج من الله تعالى وامتحان وبلية

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p124#2/r8.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p124#2/r8.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p124#2/r8.claim: Another view takes the utterance itself, rather than the blessing, as the trial.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p124#2/r8.anchor: وقيل: بل كلمته التي قالها فتنة

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p124#2/r9.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p124#2/r9.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p124#2/r9.claim: Most people do not recognize that the blessing is a test and gradual enticement.

BAYDAWI-FULL:39:49/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:49/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:49/r1.claim: This describes the human species according to its prevalent behavior; the fa connects the episode to their response when God alone is mentioned.
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:49/r1.anchor: إخبار عن الجنس بما يغلب فيه، والعطف على قوله

BAYDAWI-FULL:39:49/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:49/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:49/r2.claim: The sequence exposes their reversal: they recoil from mentioning God alone and welcome mention of idols, yet in distress pray to the one they recoiled from.
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:49/r2.anchor: لبيان مناقضتهم وتعكيسهم في التسبب بمعنى أنهم يشمئزون عن ذكر الله وحده ويستبشرون بذكر الآلهة

BAYDAWI-FULL:39:49/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:49/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:49/r3.claim: The intervening material is a parenthesis that reinforces the condemnation of this inconsistency.
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:49/r3.anchor: وما بينهما اعتراض مؤكد لإنكار ذلك عليهم

BAYDAWI-FULL:39:49/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:49/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:49/r4.claim: Khawwalah means that God grants the blessing as a favor; this act of granting is particular to God.
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:49/r4.anchor: أعطيناه إياه تفضلا فإن التخويل مختص به

BAYDAWI-FULL:39:49/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:49/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:49/r5.claim: One interpretation is that the speaker claims to know the means by which he earned the blessing.

BAYDAWI-FULL:39:49/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:49/r6.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:49/r6.claim: Alternatively, he claims he knew he would receive it because he deserved it.
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:49/r6.anchor: أو بأني سأعطاه لما لي من استحقاقه

BAYDAWI-FULL:39:49/r7.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:49/r7.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:49/r7.claim: A further interpretation is that he attributes the gift to God's knowledge of his deserving it.

BAYDAWI-FULL:39:49/r8.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:49/r8.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:49/r8.claim: The pronoun refers to mā if that is relative; otherwise it refers to the blessing, with masculine agreement because the intended referent is a thing from it.
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:49/r8.anchor: والهاء فيه لما إن جعلت موصولة وإلا فللنعمة والتذكير لأن المراد شيء منها

BAYDAWI-FULL:39:49/r9.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:49/r9.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:49/r9.claim: The blessing is a test of whether its recipient will be grateful or ungrateful, refuting his claim that it proves his merit.
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:49/r9.anchor: امتحان له أيشكر أم يكفر، وهو رد لما قاله

BAYDAWI-FULL:39:49/r10.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:49/r10.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:49/r10.claim: The feminine pronoun agrees either with the predicate or with the word niʿma; a masculine reading is also reported.
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:49/r10.anchor: الخير أو لفظ ال { نعمة } ، وقرىء بالتذكير

BAYDAWI-FULL:39:49/r11.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:49/r11.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:49/r11.claim: Most people do not know that the blessing is a test; this confirms that the human is used generically.
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:49/r11.anchor: ذلك، وهو دليل على أن الإنسان للجنس

BIQAI-FULL:v6p458/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p458/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p458/r7.claim: He explains the shift to this example by their strange habit of repaying beneficence with evil, though they ought to do the opposite.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p458/r7.anchor: وهو مجازاة الإحسان بالإساءة وقد كانوا جديرين بضده

BIQAI-FULL:v6p458/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p458/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p458/r8.claim: الإنسان generalizes the pattern to the human type, and ضر means any harm, including harm from a source one would expect; he links the wording to the opening of this sūra.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p458/r8.anchor: أي ضر كان من جهة يتوقعها كما تقدم في التي في أول السورة

BIQAI-FULL:v6p458/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p458/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p458/r9.claim: He allows the example to follow either the preceding ransom scene or the unbelievers’ aversion to mentioning God: despite their dislike of His remembrance and delight in idols, distress makes them call on Him alone.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p458/r9.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون مسببا عن الإخبار بافتدائهم بما يقدرون عليه وأن يكون مسببا عن اشمئزازهم من توحيد الله

BIQAI-FULL:v6p458/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p458/r10.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p458/r10.claim: In distress they call God, recognizing His greatness rather than their idols, even though they recoil from mention of Him and rejoice when idols are mentioned; most people acknowledge truth only under harm.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p458/r10.anchor: عالما بعظمتنا دون آلهته مع اشمئزازه من ذكرنا واستبشاره بذكرها

BIQAI-FULL:v6p458/r11.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p458/r11.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p458/r11.claim: The delayed ثم signals the severity and duration of the harm, making his quick forgetfulness of it especially blameworthy.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p458/r11.anchor: أشار إلى عظمته وطول زمنه بأداة التراخي

BIQAI-FULL:v6p458/r12.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p458/r12.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p458/r12.claim: God grants the blessing out of sheer beneficence, cares for him, and makes it fit his condition despite his having done nothing to earn it.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p458/r12.anchor: أي أعطيناه على عظمتنا متفضلين عليه محسنين القيام بأمره

BIQAI-FULL:v6p458/r13.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p458/r13.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p458/r13.claim: The blessing comes entirely from God; no one else has any share in it.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p458/r13.anchor: ليس لأحد غيرنا فيها شائبة من ولولا عظمتنا ما كانت

BIQAI-FULL:v6p458/r14.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p458/r14.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p458/r14.claim: He forgets even prolonged hardship, appropriates the gift to himself, and does not learn to thank its giver; the masculine pronoun magnifies the blessing.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p458/r14.anchor: ناسيا لما كان فيه من الضر وإن كان قد طال أمده

BIQAI-FULL:v6p458/r15.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p458/r15.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p458/r15.claim: The passive verb signals that he does not care to identify or thank the giver; he attends instead to the gift’s greatness and his own self-importance.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p458/r15.anchor: وبنى الفعل للمجهول إشارة إلى أنه لا نظر له في تعرف المعطي من هو يشكره

BIQAI-FULL:v6p458/r16.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p458/r16.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p458/r16.claim: He claims the great gift is proportionate to his own greatness, as though he gives to himself according to his own measure.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p458/r16.anchor: لأني عظيم فأنا أعطي على مقداري

BIQAI-FULL:v6p458/r17.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p458/r17.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p458/r17.claim: He parses ما as an added particle that blocks إن and gives an exclusive sense; alternatively, ما is a relative pronoun as the subject of إن, with على علم as its predicate.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p458/r17.anchor: و ( ما ) هي الزائدة الكافة لأن للدلالة على الحصر

BIQAI-FULL:v6p458/r18.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p458/r18.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p458/r18.claim: On the alternative parse, he says the gift came through great knowledge earned by effort, seeking, and scheming, or through God’s knowledge that he deserved it.

BIQAI-FULL:v6p458/r19.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p458/r19.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p458/r19.claim: The blessing is instead a trial that tests gratitude against ingratitude and establishes the proof; if it leads to Hell, it is a form of gradual entrapment.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p458/r19.anchor: لاختباره هل يشكر أم يكفر لتقام عليه الحجة

BIQAI-FULL:v6p458/r20.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p458/r20.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p458/r20.claim: The feminine pronoun belittles the gift relative to God’s power and its outcome of delusion, whereas the earlier masculine pronoun had magnified it as something deserving gratitude.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p458/r20.anchor: وأنث الضمير تحقيرا لها بالنسبة إلى قدرته سبحانه وتعالى ولأنها أدت إلى الغرور بعد أن ذكر ضميرها أولا تعظيما لها

BIQAI-FULL:v6p458/r21.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p458/r21.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p458/r21.claim: Most of these speakers acquire no knowledge because they are innately coarse and ignorant; even if God answered their call in Hell and blessed them, they would credit someone else as they do in this life.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p458/r21.anchor: فلو أنهم إذا دعونا وهم في جهنم أجبناهم وأنعمنا عليهم نعمتنا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p33/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p33/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p33/r6.claim: The فاء branches from the reaction to hearing God's name alone in 39:45, with intervening linked asides; the striking contrast is that they shun God's name yet call Him alone in distress.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p33/r6.anchor: الفاء لتفريع هذا الكلام على قوله

IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p33/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p33/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p33/r7.claim: This is a sequence of reported episodes rather than worldly causation; unlike the similar opening in 39:8, it begins with فاء. The main consequence is the distress prayer; what follows elaborates it.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p33/r7.anchor: وهذه النكتة هي الفارقة بين العطف بالفاء هنا وعطف نظيرها بالواو في قوله أول السورة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p35/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p35/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p35/r1.claim: As in 39:8, الإنسان means the class of polytheists, a generic definite with customary collective scope; the variation makes the repeated passage add something new.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p35/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p35/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p35/r2.claim: إنما combines إن with the particle that neutralizes it, yielding restriction like ما...إلا: he claims he received the blessing only through his own knowledge of how to acquire it.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p35/r2.anchor: إنما } فيه هي الكلمة المركبة من ( إن ) الكافة التي تصير كلمة تدل على الحصر بمنزلة ( ما ) النافية التي بعدها ( إلا ) الاستثنائية

IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p35/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p35/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p35/r3.claim: The pronoun in أوتيته returns to نعمة, treated as something present before the speaker, so the pronoun functions like a demonstrative; Ibn Ashur compares 46:24.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p35/r3.anchor: وتركيز ضمير الغائب في قوله : { أوتيته } عائد إلى { نعمة } على تأويل حكاية مقالتهم بأنها صادرة منهم في حال حضور ما بين أيديهم من أنواع النعم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p35/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p35/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p35/r4.claim: Their statement expresses what they actually believe, since speech follows belief; على gives the cause, meaning that the blessing came because of their knowledge.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p35/r4.anchor: اعتقد ذلك فجرى في أقواله إذ القول على وفق الاعتقاد

IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p35/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p35/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p35/r5.claim: Here knowledge means ordinary acumen and planning, common to practical people; in the Qarun passage it means his special knowledge of gold and silver craft and alchemy that built his wealth.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p35/r5.anchor: لأن المراد بالعلم هنا مجرد الفطنة والتدبير

IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p35/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p35/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p35/r6.claim: The supposed knowledge is skill at earning and warding off harm, like a sailor's maneuvering in a dangerous sea; the boast answers believers who attribute the blessing to God's favor.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p35/r6.anchor: والمراد : العلم بطرق الكسب ودفع الضر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p36/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p36/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p36/r1.claim: بل cancels their claim: God gives blessings to reveal how grateful people are, making the blessing a trial of their knowledge of Him and gratitude, though God needs no test to know them.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p36/r1.anchor: وضمير { هي } عائد إلى القول المستفاد من { قال } على طريقة إعادة الضمير على المصدر المأخوذ من فعل نحو

IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p36/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p36/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p36/r2.claim: هي may refer to the statement inferred from قال, to the word understood as a sentence, or to the blessing; the statement can cause a trial or arise from one.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p36/r2.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون الضمير عائدا إلى نعمة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p36/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p36/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p36/r3.claim: Most people, including the speakers, do not realize that worldly blessings can test their response, with ingratitude potentially leading to disbelief.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p36/r3.anchor: لكن لا يعلم أكثر الناس ومنهم القائلون

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p535#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p535#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p535#2/r1.claim: The verse exposes idolaters’ inconsistency: in distress they abandon their idols and call on the Creator of heaven and earth.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p535#2/r1.anchor: هذه حجة تلزم عباد الأوثان التناقض في أعمالهم، وذلك أنهم يعبدون الأوثان

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p535#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p535#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p535#2/r2.claim: Al-insān here denotes the human kind generally.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p535#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p535#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p535#2/r3.claim: Khawwalnāhu means that God granted the person possession of something.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p535#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p535#2/r4.speaker: الزجاج وغيره
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p535#2/r4.claim: Al-Zajjaj and others define takhwīl as a gift given without recompense.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p535#2/r4.anchor: قال الزجاج وغيره: التخويل: العطاء عن غير مجازاة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p535#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p535#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p535#2/r5.claim: The blessing is general, including relief from distress, health, security, and wealth; 39:52 also indicates its breadth.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p535#2/r5.anchor: والنعمة هنا: عامة في جميع ما يسديه الله إلى العبد، فمن ذلك إزالة الضر المذكور

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p535#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p535#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p535#2/r6.claim: The pronoun may refer to wealth, to the named blessing whose generic noun includes masculine and feminine referents, or to the relative meaning of mā in innamā.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p535#2/r6.anchor: وذلك يحتمل وجوها، منها: أن يريد بالنعمة المال كما قدمناه، ومنها أن يعيد الضمير على المذكور

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p535#2/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p535#2/r7.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p535#2/r7.claim: If mā is restrictive, ʿalā ʿilmin is an accusative circumstantial phrase; if mā is relative, it is the predicate of inna and indicates an omitted predicate.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p535#2/r7.anchor: في موضع نصب على الحال مع أن تكون «ما» كافة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p535#2/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p535#2/r8.speaker: قتادة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p535#2/r8.claim: Qatada takes the claim to mean that the person gained the blessing through his own knowledge of business and other means of earning; this reflects self-admiration.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p535#2/r8.anchor: يحتمل أن يريد على علم مني بوجه المكاسب والتجارات وغير ذلك، قاله قتادة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p535#2/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p535#2/r9.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p535#2/r9.claim: Alternatively, the person boasts of prior divine knowledge and an entitlement secured with God, a delusion that nothing can harm him.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p535#2/r9.anchor: ويحتمل أن يريد على علم من الله في، وشيء سبق لي، واستحقاق حزته عند الله لا يضرني معه شيء

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p535#2/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p535#2/r10.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p535#2/r10.claim: God corrects the boast: the blessing is instead a trial for its recipient.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p535#2/r10.anchor: بل هي فتنة أي ليس الأمر كما قال، بل هذه الفعلة به فتنة له وابتلاء

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p188#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p188#2/r1.speaker: مقاتل
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p188#2/r1.claim: Muqatil identifies the “human” here as Abu Hudhayfa ibn al-Mughira and points to the parallel at 39:8.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p188#2/r1.anchor: قال مقاتل هو أبو حذيفة ابن المغيرة وقد سبق في هذه السورة نظيرها الزمر 8

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p188#2/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p188#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p188#2/r2.claim: The blessing is expressed as “I was given it” because what is meant is the act of conferring the blessing.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p188#2/r2.anchor: وإنما كنى عن النعمة بقوله ﴿ أوتيته ﴾ لأن المراد بالنعمة الإنعام

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p188#2/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p188#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p188#2/r3.claim: One explanation takes the boast to mean that he received it for good that God knew to be in him.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p188#2/r3.anchor: ﴿ على علم ﴾ عندي أي على خير علمه الله عندي

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p188#2/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p188#2/r4.speaker: قيل
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p188#2/r4.claim: Another explanation is that God knew the speaker deserved the blessing.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p188#2/r4.anchor: وقيل على علم من الله بأني له أهل

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p188#2/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p188#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p188#2/r5.claim: “Rather, it is a trial” refers to the blessing God bestowed.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p188#2/r5.anchor: قال الله تعالى ﴿ بل هي ﴾ يعني النعمة التي أنعم الله عليه بها

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p188#2/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p188#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p188#2/r6.claim: The blessing tests the servant, who may respond with gratitude or ingratitude.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p188#2/r6.anchor: أي بلوى يبتلى بها العبد ليشكر أو يكفر

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p188#2/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p188#2/r7.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p188#2/r7.claim: Most people fail to know that this is a test and a gradual entrapment for them.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p188#2/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p188#2/r8.speaker: قيل
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p188#2/r8.claim: A further view takes “it” as the boastful statement itself, which is a trial.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p188#2/r8.anchor: وقيل بل هي أي المقالة التي قالها فتنة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p105/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p105/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p105/r1.claim: In hardship a person humbly turns to God, but after receiving a favor may become arrogant and claim it came from his own merit and special standing with God.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p105/r1.anchor: أنه في حال الضراء يضرع إلى الله، عز وجل، وينيب إليه ويدعوه

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p105/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p105/r2.speaker: قتادة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p105/r2.claim: Qatādah glosses the boast as meaning the person received the favor because of good or merit he possesses.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p105/r2.anchor: قال قتادة: {على علم عندي} على خير عندي

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p105/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p105/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p105/r3.claim: The favor is a test of whether its recipient obeys or disobeys, notwithstanding God's prior knowledge of the outcome.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p105/r3.anchor: أنعمنا عليه بهذه النعمة لنختبره فيما أنعمنا عليه، أيطيع أم يعصي؟ مع علمنا المتقدم بذلك

JISHUMI:v8p6077/r14.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p6077/r14.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v8p6077/r14.claim: One claim of knowledge means that God approved of the speaker and therefore gave him blessings.
JISHUMI:v8p6077/r14.anchor: قيل: علم برضاه عني؛ فلذلك أعطاني ما أولاني من النعم

JISHUMI:v8p6077/r15.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p6077/r15.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v8p6077/r15.claim: Another claim means that God knew the speaker was deserving of the blessing.
JISHUMI:v8p6077/r15.anchor: وقيل: على علم من الله بأني له أهل

JISHUMI:v8p6077/r16.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p6077/r16.speaker: قتادة
JISHUMI:v8p6077/r16.claim: Qatada explains the claim as knowledge the speaker already possessed.
JISHUMI:v8p6077/r16.anchor: وقيل: على خبر عندي، عن قتادة

JISHUMI:v8p6077/r17.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p6077/r17.speaker: الحسن، وأبو علي
JISHUMI:v8p6077/r17.claim: Al-Hasan and Abu ʿAli explain the claim as personal knowledge of strength, ingenuity, and ways of earning.
JISHUMI:v8p6077/r17.anchor: وقيل: على علم لي من الجلد والحيل ووجوه المكاسب، عن الحسن، وأبي علي

JISHUMI:v8p6077/r18.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p6077/r18.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v8p6077/r18.claim: The statement exposes their ignorance about who grants benefits and harms.
JISHUMI:v8p6077/r18.anchor: فأشار إلى جهلهم بدفع المنافع والمضار وممن هي

JISHUMI:v8p6077/r19.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p6077/r19.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v8p6077/r19.claim: The blessing is a test because it obliges gratitude and fulfillment of God’s rights.
JISHUMI:v8p6077/r19.anchor: قيل: النعمة فتنة؛ أي: امتحان من حيث توجب الشكر وحقوق الله تعالى

JISHUMI:v8p6077/r20.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p6077/r20.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v8p6077/r20.claim: Another explanation says blessings become punishment when people attribute them to themselves.
JISHUMI:v8p6077/r20.anchor: وقيل: النعم فتنة؛ أي: عذاب لهم إذا أضافوها إلى أنفسهم

JISHUMI:v8p6077/r21.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p6077/r21.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v8p6077/r21.claim: A further explanation treats knowledge as a test: acting on it earns reward, while failing to act makes it evidence against one.
JISHUMI:v8p6077/r21.anchor: وقيل: العلوم فتنة، من عمل بها كانت مثوبة، ومن لم يعمل بها كانت حجة عليه

JISHUMI:v8p6077/r22.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p6077/r22.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v8p6077/r22.claim: Another view says the very phrase they utter is a trial.
JISHUMI:v8p6077/r22.anchor: وقيل: هذه الكلمة التي قالها فتنة

JISHUMI:v8p6077/r23.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p6077/r23.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v8p6077/r23.claim: They do not know what blessings require of them in gratitude.
JISHUMI:v8p6077/r23.anchor: قيل: لا يعلمون مواضع النعمة وما يجب فيها من الشكر

JISHUMI:v8p6077/r24.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p6077/r24.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v8p6077/r24.claim: They do not understand the consequences of their own affairs.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p136/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p136/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p136/r1.claim: Takhwīl is exclusively a favor: خولني means giving someone something without compensation.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p136/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p136/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p136/r2.claim: One possible claim is that the recipient knew he would be given this because of his merit and entitlement.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p136/r2.anchor: على علم مني أني سأعطاه ، لما في من فضل

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p136/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p136/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p136/r3.claim: Alternatively, the speaker means God knows him and knows he deserves the gift.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p136/r3.anchor: أو على علم من الله بي وباستحقاقي

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p136/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p136/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p136/r4.claim: A third possibility is that the speaker attributes the gift to his own knowledge of how to earn wealth, like Qarun’s boast in 28:78.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p136/r4.anchor: على علم مني بوجوه الكسب ، كما قال قارون

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p136/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p136/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p136/r5.claim: The masculine pronoun in أوتيته treats نعمة as a thing or portion of blessings in sense; alternatively, ما in إنما is a relative pronoun to which it refers.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p136/r5.anchor: ذهابا به إلى المعنى ؛ لأن قوله : { نعمة منا } شيئا

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p136/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p136/r6.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p136/r6.claim: The reply rejects the claim: the gift is instead a test of whether its recipient will be grateful or ungrateful.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p136/r6.anchor: إنكار لقوله كأنه قال : ما خولناك من خولناك من النعمة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p136/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p136/r7.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p136/r7.claim: The pronoun shifts from masculine to feminine first by meaning and then by the wording فتنة; a feminine predicate licenses the feminine subject, as in ما جاءت حاجتك.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p136/r7.anchor: حملا على المعنى أولا ، وعلى اللفظ آخرا ؛ ولأن الخبر

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p136/r8.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p136/r8.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p136/r8.claim: A variant reads بل هو فتنة, matching the masculine construction of إنما أوتيته.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p136/r8.anchor: وقرىء : ( بل هو فتنة ) وفق { إنما أوتيته }

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p136/r9.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p136/r9.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p136/r9.claim: The ف here connects the distress prayer to the earlier recoil from God’s mention and delight in mentioning idols at 39:45; the intervening verses are an aside that reinforces the rebuke, unlike the parallel opening passage at 39:8, which is simply coordinated with what precedes.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p136/r9.anchor: السبب في ذلك أن هذه وقعت مسببة عن قوله : { وإذا ذكر الله وحده اشمأزت }

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p136/r10.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p136/r10.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p136/r10.claim: Although disgust at God would seem to prompt avoidance, the ف treats the disbeliever’s appeal in hardship as if his denial caused the same appeal that faith causes, thereby exposing and censuring his inconsistency.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p136/r10.anchor: في هذه التسبيب لطف ، وبيانه أن تقول : زيد مؤمن بالله

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p136/r11.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p136/r11.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p136/r11.claim: The subsequent prayer in 39:46 and threat in 39:47 further underscore the rejection of those who recoil from God yet turn to Him in hardship; the same sequence is contrasted with the earlier passage at 39:8.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p136/r11.anchor: ثم ما عقبه من الوعيد العظيم : تأكيد لإنكار اشمئزازهم واستبشارهم

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p130/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p130/r1.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p130/r1.claim: The verse is said to have been revealed concerning Abu Hudhayfa ibn al-Mughira.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p130/r1.anchor: قيل إنها نزلت في أبي حذيفة . ابن المعيرة .

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p130/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p130/r2.speaker: ابن عيسى
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p130/r2.claim: Ibn Isa says the speaker attributes the favor to God's satisfaction.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p130/r2.anchor: أحدها : على علم برضاه عني , قاله ابن عيسى

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p130/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p130/r3.speaker: مجاهد
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p130/r3.claim: Mujahid says the speaker attributes it to his own knowledge.

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p130/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p130/r4.speaker: الحسن
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p130/r4.claim: Al-Hasan says he means knowledge God taught him.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p130/r4.anchor: الثالث : بعلم علمني الله إياه , قاله الحسن

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p130/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p130/r5.speaker: النقاش
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p130/r5.claim: Al-Naqqash says the meaning is “I knew I would receive it.”
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p130/r5.anchor: الرابع : علمت أني سوف أصيبه : حكاه النقاش

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p130/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p130/r6.speaker: قتادة
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p130/r6.claim: Qatada says the meaning is “according to information I had.”
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p130/r6.anchor: الخامس : على خبر عندي , قاله قتادة

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p130/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p130/r7.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p130/r7.claim: The trial may be the blessing itself, which tests its recipient.

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p130/r8.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p130/r8.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p130/r8.claim: Alternatively, it is the person's claim about the favor, for which he is punished.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p130/r8.anchor: الثاني : المقالة التي اعتقدها لأنه يعاقب عليها

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p130/r9.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p130/r9.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p130/r9.claim: Most people do not recognize that apparent blessings are a test.

MUJAHID:v2p559/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v2p559/r1.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v2p559/r1.claim: Mujahid explains khawwalnāhu as “We gave him.”
MUJAHID:v2p559/r1.anchor: عن ابن أبي نجيح عن مجاهد ﴿ ثم إذا خولناه ﴾ يعني أعطيناه

MUJAHID:v2p559/r2.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v2p559/r2.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v2p559/r2.claim: Mujahid explains the claim of receiving it on account of knowledge as receiving it because of one's nobility.
MUJAHID:v2p559/r2.anchor: عن ابن أبي نجيح عن مجاهد ﴿ إنما أوتيته على علم ﴾ يقول إنما أعطيته على شرف

MUQATIL:39:49-50/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:39:49-50/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:39:49-50/r1.claim: The person called humanity here is Abū Ḥudhayfa ibn al-Mughīra; harm means trial and distress.
MUQATIL:39:49-50/r1.anchor: { فإذا مس } يعنى أصاب { الإنسان } يعنى أبا حذيفة بن المغيرة { ضر } يعنى بلاء وشدة

MUQATIL:39:49-50/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:39:49-50/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:39:49-50/r2.claim: When afflicted, he calls on God sincerely in monotheism to remove his distress.
MUQATIL:39:49-50/r2.anchor: دعا ربه منيبا يعنى مخلصا بالتوحيد أن يكشف ما به من الضر

MUQATIL:39:49-50/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:39:49-50/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:39:49-50/r3.claim: If God grants him a blessing, it means that He gives him good; the man claims he received it through knowledge he possessed.
MUQATIL:39:49-50/r3.anchor: يقول: ثم إذا آتيناه، يعنى أعطيناه الخير

MUQATIL:39:49-50/r4.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:39:49-50/r4.speaker: author
MUQATIL:39:49-50/r4.claim: The blessing is instead a trial, though most people do not know.
MUQATIL:39:49-50/r4.anchor: { بل هي فتنة } يعنى بل تلك النعمة بلاء ابتلى به { ولكن أكثرهم لا يعلمون } [آية: 49] ذلك

NASAFI-FULL:v4p58#3/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p58#3/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p58#3/r1.claim: Khawwalanāhu means giving a favor gratuitously, without compensation.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p58#3/r1.anchor: أى أعطيناه تفضلا يقال خولنى إذا أعطاك على غير جزاء

NASAFI-FULL:v4p58#3/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p58#3/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p58#3/r2.claim: Do not pause after from Us because the response to إذا is the following verb, he said.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p58#3/r2.anchor: ولا تقف عليه لأن جواب إذا

NASAFI-FULL:v4p58#3/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p58#3/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p58#3/r3.claim: They may mean the favor came from their excellence and merit, or from their knowledge of earning, as Qarun claimed.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p58#3/r3.anchor: منى أنى سأعطاه لما فى من فضل واستحقاق أو على علم منى بوجوه الكسب كما قال قارون على علم عندى

NASAFI-FULL:v4p58#3/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p58#3/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p58#3/r4.claim: The masculine suffix refers to the favor by meaning, as نعمة منا denotes a thing or portion of favor; alternatively, ما in إنما is relative and the suffix refers to it.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p58#3/r4.anchor: وإنما ذكر الضمير فى أوتيته وهو للنعمة نظرا إلى المعنى لأن قوله نعمة منا شيئا من النعمة وقسما منها وقيل ما فى إنما موصولة

NASAFI-FULL:v4p58#3/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p58#3/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p58#3/r5.claim: The correction rebukes their claim: the favor is a trial of gratitude or ingratitude.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p58#3/r5.anchor: انكار له كأنه قال ما خولناك من النعمة لما تقول بل هى فتنة أى ابتلاء وامتحان لك أتشكر أم تكفر

NASAFI-FULL:v4p58#3/r6.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p58#3/r6.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p58#3/r6.claim: The feminine predicate فتنة permits a feminine subject; the alternate reading follows the masculine reference to ما.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p58#3/r6.anchor: ولما كان الخبر مؤنثا أعنى فتنة ساغ تأنيث المبتدا لأجله

NASAFI-FULL:v4p58#3/r7.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p58#3/r7.speaker: قارئ
NASAFI-FULL:v4p58#3/r7.claim: An alternate reading has هو فتنة, following the masculine reference in إنما أوتيته.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p58#3/r7.anchor: وقرىء بل هو فتنة على وفق إنما أوتيته

NASAFI-FULL:v4p58#3/r8.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p58#3/r8.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p58#3/r8.claim: Most people do not know that the favor is a trial.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p58#3/r8.anchor: ﴿ ولكن أكثرهم لا يعلمون ﴾ أنها فتنة

NASAFI-FULL:v4p58#3/r9.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p58#3/r9.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p58#3/r9.claim: The fāء marks this as a result of their earlier recoil when God alone is mentioned: in distress they call Him, not the idols they welcome.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p58#3/r9.anchor: والسبب فى عطف هذه الآية بالفاء وعطف مثلها فى أول السورة بالواو أن هذه وقعت مسببة عن قوله وإذا ذكر الله وحده اشمأزت

NASAFI-FULL:v4p58#3/r10.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p58#3/r10.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p58#3/r10.claim: Intervening verses are an aside reinforcing the rebuke through the Prophet's supplication and the severe warning.

NASAFI-FULL:v4p58#3/r11.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p58#3/r11.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p58#3/r11.claim: The first occurrence in the sūra uses واو because its clause merely follows a related clause; فاء here signals causation.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p58#3/r11.anchor: وأما الآية الأولى فلم تقع مسببة وما هى إلا جملة ناسبت جملة قبلها فعطفت عليها بالواو

NASAFI-FULL:v4p58#3/r12.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p58#3/r12.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p58#3/r12.claim: The contrast says a believer's distress leads him to God, while the disbeliever also turns to God, as if his disbelief were treated as belief in this appeal.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p58#3/r12.anchor: ثم تقول زيد كافر بالله فاذا مسه ضر التجأ إليه فتجىء بالفاء مجيئك بها ثمة كأن الكافر حين التجأ إلى الله التجاء المؤمن إليه

QURTUBI-FULL:39:49-52/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:39:49-52/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:39:49-52/r1.claim: One report says this verse was revealed concerning Hudhayfa ibn al-Mughira.
QURTUBI-FULL:39:49-52/r1.anchor: قيل: إنها نزلت في حذيفة بن المغيرة.

QURTUBI-FULL:39:49-52/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:39:49-52/r2.speaker: قتادة
QURTUBI-FULL:39:49-52/r2.claim: Qatada says the person claims to have received the blessing through his own knowledge of ways to earn money.
QURTUBI-FULL:39:49-52/r2.anchor: قال قتادة: { على علم } عندي بوجوه المكاسب

QURTUBI-FULL:39:49-52/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:39:49-52/r3.speaker: قتادة
QURTUBI-FULL:39:49-52/r3.claim: Qatada also reports an interpretation that the speaker means he received it because of good fortune he possesses.
QURTUBI-FULL:39:49-52/r3.anchor: وعنه أيضا { على علم } على خير عندي.

QURTUBI-FULL:39:49-52/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:39:49-52/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:39:49-52/r4.claim: Another explanation is that the speaker claims God knows his merit and therefore gave him the blessing.
QURTUBI-FULL:39:49-52/r4.anchor: وقيل: { على علم } أي على علم من الله بفضلي.

QURTUBI-FULL:39:49-52/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:39:49-52/r5.speaker: الحسن
QURTUBI-FULL:39:49-52/r5.claim: Al-Hasan says the speaker means he received it through knowledge God taught him.
QURTUBI-FULL:39:49-52/r5.anchor: وقال الحسن: { على علم } أي بعلم علمني الله إياه.

QURTUBI-FULL:39:49-52/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:39:49-52/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:39:49-52/r6.claim: One explanation is that the person thinks his worldly allotment shows that he holds a rank with God.
QURTUBI-FULL:39:49-52/r6.anchor: وقيل: المعنى أنه قال قد علمت أني إذا أوتيت هذا في الدنيا أن لي عند الله منزلة

QURTUBI-FULL:39:49-52/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:39:49-52/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:39:49-52/r7.claim: God corrects him: the blessings given are a trial by which he is tested.
QURTUBI-FULL:39:49-52/r7.anchor: فقال الله: { بل هي فتنة } أي بل النعم التي أوتيتها فتنة تختبر بها.

QURTUBI-FULL:39:49-52/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:39:49-52/r8.speaker: الفراء
QURTUBI-FULL:39:49-52/r8.claim: Al-Farraʾ says hi is feminine because fitnah is feminine, though huwa fitnah would also be grammatical.
QURTUBI-FULL:39:49-52/r8.anchor: قال الفراء: أنث «هي» لتأنيث الفتنة، ولو كان بل هو فتنة لجاز.

QURTUBI-FULL:39:49-52/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:39:49-52/r9.speaker: النحاس
QURTUBI-FULL:39:49-52/r9.claim: Al-Nahhas supplies the omitted wording: rather, I gave it to him as a trial.

QURTUBI-FULL:39:49-52/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:39:49-52/r10.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:39:49-52/r10.claim: Most people do not understand that being given wealth is a test.
QURTUBI-FULL:39:49-52/r10.anchor: أي لا يعلمون أن إعطاءهم المال اختبار
